action: No action needed; for awareness. Hotel and retail operators should keep reservation and payment systems segmented and backed up so one ransomware infection cannot halt bookings.
date_note: Date Keio disclosed the revenue impact (as reported by Business+IT); the ransomware attack itself was confirmed on 26 September 2026.
exec: A ransomware attack on a major Japanese rail and hotel group has halted hotel bookings for weeks and is expected to cost about 1.8 billion yen in hotel income.
plain: Keio, the Japanese rail and hotel group, was hit by ransomware in September. New bookings at its Keio Presso Inn hotels are still suspended, and it expects to lose about 1.8 billion yen of hotel income.
summary: Keio Corporation said on 17 November that a ransomware attack, confirmed on its group servers in the early hours of 26 September, will cut Keio Presso Inn accommodation income by about 1.8 billion yen over October to December. New bookings at the hotels remain suspended, with reopening planned around December. Keio says personal data may have leaked. Business+IT reports outside experts hired by Keio pointed to Qilin; Keio did not name a group.
title: Keio Corporation expects 1.8 billion yen hotel income loss after September ransomware attack

validation.note: Business+IT (17 Nov, free part of article) and BleepingComputer (28 Sep) read; both report the 26 September ransomware attack on Keio. Keio's own release PDF was linked but not opened. The Qilin link is Business+IT's relay of a KSB News report, not read.
